studies.label: Classroom factorial RCT: causal-reasoning training and ChatGPT Edu access
studies.cluster_se_treatment: Classes were randomized within bachelor program. Appendix Section 1 specifies one intact class per program per arm, with an additional Management class assigned to Causal&GPT; it describes three programs and 13 classes. Separate numeric arm totals for clusters are not printed, so they remain null under the transcription-only rule. This allocation establishes multiple randomized classes in every arm. PDF p. 17 (printed p. 16), Appendix Section 1. Standard errors cluster by mother tongue x high-school type x degree class, explicitly 50 clusters in Tables A.12-A.14. Appendix Section 4 defines class as the class section and says these variables create the clustering cells. These cells subdivide assignment classes; the paper does not report SEs clustered at the randomization-class level. PDF p. 37 (printed p. 36), Appendix Section 4; PDF p. 46 (printed p. 45), Table A.12 note; PDF p. 47 (printed p. 46), Table A.13 note; PDF p. 48 (printed p. 47), Table A.14 note.

arms.name: Control
arms.description: Placebo business game without causal-reasoning instruction or feedback; no AI during the merchandising case.

arms.name: Causal
arms.description: Causal-reasoning training game with examples and feedback, followed by a reminder to use the learned skills; no AI during the merchandising case.

arms.name: GPT
arms.description: Placebo business game followed by access to ChatGPT Edu through an institutional subscription in a separate browser tab during the merchandising case.

arms.name: Causal&GPT
arms.description: Causal-reasoning training game and reminder, plus ChatGPT Edu access during the merchandising case.

studies.task: Write a consultant-style recommendation to increase alumni awareness and usage of university merchandise, using the supplied business case.

estimates.notes: Higher scores mean more effective marketing recommendations, the usefulness dimension; this is not an originality or overall-creativity rating. The paper calls the human evaluations its main results, but preregistered outcome priority cannot be verified. The GPT coefficient compares GPT with Control at Causal = 0 in the factorial model; it is not the average AI effect across training conditions. The interaction coefficient is not a direct contrast involving the combined arm. The model uses all experimental arms; its printed observation count is retained in regression.model. n_total is null because a total for the two named arms is not printed, and counts have not been added. Arm means and arm SDs are not reported. Regression constants are not transcribed as arm means; Table A.7 reports whole-sample descriptive statistics. se_basis = cluster describes the paper's clustering cells, which subdivide the randomized classes; assignment-class clustered precision is not reported. Specifications from this study share participants and are not independent estimates.

open_items: Arm-level means, SDs and mean uncertainty are not printed for the outcomes. Table A.7 gives only whole-sample summaries; raw regression outcomes were not standardized before estimation. Those SDs must not be substituted for control-arm or two-arm pooled SDs.

The paper reports clustering cells defined by mother tongue, high-school type and class, rather than randomization-class clustered inference. Proper precision for pooling requires assignment-class analysis. se_basis = cluster does not establish that this requirement is met.

Per-arm randomized cluster totals are not separately printed as numerals. Appendix Section 1 specifies the allocation across programs; that description is retained in cluster_se_treatment and numeric totals are left null rather than calculated.

No combined-arm direct contrast or covariance needed for coefficient sums is printed. In particular, the interaction is not the effect of adding GPT after causal training or the effect of training when GPT is available.

Within-solution diversity and the PDS models using it omit the single-idea responses. Their arm memberships and arm-specific analyzed counts are not printed. No full-study arm counts are assigned to these reduced-sample models.
Two-arm total participant counts are not printed. n_total is therefore null; the reported all-arm model observation count appears in regression.model with a source for the observation row.
The between-solution diversity measure refers to the pooled sample across all arms. Arm-specific internal diversity, arm levels and exact weighting over ideas are not printed.
The AEA preregistration identifier/link is withheld. Preregistered primary-outcome status cannot be confirmed even though the paper identifies the human performance evaluation as its main result.

The trial country is not explicitly stated; country remains null. The appendix names Bocconi in the scenario and administrative-record descriptions, but this is not treated as an explicit trial-country statement.
The assistance model release year is not stated. ai_tool.year is null; the November 2025 experiment date in Appendix Section 1 is not substituted for a release year.
The main text describes a case lasting 45 minutes, whereas Appendix Section 1 describes the whole session as approximately 45 minutes. A separate case-only duration cannot be confirmed.
No shared participant sample with another paper is reported. shared_sample = null records absence of confirmed overlap, not independently verified sample uniqueness.
notes: Extraction A read the entire markdown conversion, including appendices and references, and checked cited PDF pages with PyMuPDF text extraction. Tables A.9-A.14 were also passed to find_tables; no tables were detected, so their directly extracted text supplied rows and columns. Only the named extraction file is written. No effects, SEs, intervals, arm means, arm totals or standardized effects were calculated; significance bounds follow printed stars. The study includes the participating students assigned during ordinary class attendance; a census of everyone enrolled in the randomized classes is not separately reported. The paper's assignment statement and Table A.8 support the study-level arm counts. Alternative OLS and PDS specifications are preserved as separate, explicitly labeled records of the same contrasts; they share outcomes and participants. PDS models condition on post-treatment output characteristics and should not replace the baseline OLS total-effect comparisons. The expert-alignment outcome is split into its separate reference measures under S1-O5. No delayed unassisted outcome is reported. The numeric estimate fields use the printed raw-table coefficients, except the coherent-logic paper_effect, which transcribes the explicitly approximate standardized value from prose. The PDF page index plus one is used in locators, with the differing printed page number in parentheses.
